rule: All SQLAlchemy models must be defined before any foreign‑key references to them. Place every model class in app/models/ and import them in app/models/__init__.py so Base.metadata includes each table. WRONG: class Order(Base): user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('users.id')) (User defined later). RIGHT: define User first or import User before Order. This prevents missing‑table errors.

All imports must be absolute, start with app/, and reference an existing file or package that is listed in requirements.txt. WRONG: from utils import helper (relative, missing). RIGHT: from app.utils import helper and ensure the utils package is in requirements.txt. This prevents missing‑module runtime errors.

When a SQLAlchemy model defines a ForeignKey, the referenced table name must exactly match an existing model's __tablename__. WRONG: class Order(Base): user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('users.id'))  # User model uses __tablename__ = 'user'. RIGHT: class Order(Base): user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('user.id')). Verify the target table exists before running migrations.

Each route module must define and export a variable whose name matches the resource prefix and ends with _router. WRONG: router = APIRouter() in users.py. RIGHT: users_router = APIRouter(). The variable must be imported in main.py using the exact name.

Every directory that appears in an import path must contain an __init__.py file. WRONG: app/models/user.py without app/models/__init__.py. RIGHT: add an empty __init__.py in app/models/. This ensures Python treats the folder as a package and prevents ModuleNotFoundError.

Every external library used in the generated code MUST be imported at the top of the file with its exact package name. WRONG: `import orm` (undefined). RIGHT: `from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String`. Missing imports cause ModuleNotFoundError at runtime.

All SQLAlchemy models MUST inherit from the same declarative Base imported from a single `database.py` file, and a FastAPI dependency `get_db` must be used for session handling. WRONG: defining `Base = declarative_base()` in each model file. RIGHT: `from .database import Base, get_db` and using `db: Session = Depends(get_db)`. Consistent Base and session prevent SQLAlchemy errors.

Every route file MUST define a variable named exactly <resource>_router (e.g. user_router) and export it. WRONG: router = APIRouter(). RIGHT: user_router = APIRouter(). Using a generic name like `router` prevents the main app from importing the router correctly, causing RouterExportMismatch failures.

Every SQLAlchemy model must define a `__tablename__` string and any `ForeignKey` must reference an existing table name. WRONG: class Order(Base): user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('user.id')). RIGHT: class Order(Base): __tablename__ = 'orders'; user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('users.id')). This avoids SQLAlchemyError and NoReferencedTableError.

All route modules must reside in the `app/routes/` package, be listed in `app/routes/__init__.py`, and be imported in `app/main.py` using the exact module name. WRONG: from app.routes.user import router. RIGHT: from app.routes.user_routes import user_router. This guarantees the import path exists and prevents ModuleNotFoundError.

Every route module MUST define and export a variable named exactly <resource>_router (e.g. user_router). WRONG: router = APIRouter(); __all__ = [] . RIGHT: user_router = APIRouter(); __all__ = ["user_router"]. This guarantees the main app can import the router without silent failures.

All imports must be absolute within the project package and any third‑party library used must be listed in requirements.txt. WRONG: import foo (where foo is a local file not in PYTHONPATH). RIGHT: from app.utils import foo and ensure "foo" is in requirements.txt if external. This prevents missing‑module crashes at runtime.

Wrap every direct SQLAlchemy session operation in a try/except block that catches SQLAlchemyError and raises an HTTPException with status_code=500 and a concise message. WRONG: db.add(obj); db.commit(). RIGHT: try: db.add(obj); db.commit() except SQLAlchemyError as e: db.rollback(); raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Database error") . This prevents uncaught DB errors from bubbling up as 500 crashes.
